depop.seller_fee: 0% selling fee in US (since 2024-07-18) and UK. Payment processing: US 3.3% + $0.45 per transaction on the full amount the buyer pays (item + shipping + tax); UK 2.9% + £0.30. Sellers outside US/UK may still pay a 10% selling fee. Boosted listings 12% of sale (from 2026-03-23).

vinted_uk.seller_fee: None. Buyer pays Buyer Protection fee: '3% to 8% + £0.3 to £0.8' of item/bundle price, plus VAT. Item verification £10 (buyer-paid). Bumps/Showcase priced at checkout.

vinted_ireland.seller_fee: None. Buyer Protection fee 'usually 5% + €0.70' plus VAT. Price list last updated 2026-07-22.

ebay_us.seller_fee: Clothing, Shoes & Accessories: 13.6% of total sale up to $7,500 + 2.35% of the portion over $7,500; per-order fee $0.30 (orders <=$10) or $0.40 (>$10). Athletic shoes: 8% and no per-order fee if sale >= $150, else 13.6%. Women's bags & handbags: 15% if <= $2,000, 9% if > $2,000. 250 free listings/month, then $0.35 each.

ebay_uk_private.seller_fee: UK-based private sellers: no final value fee, no regulatory operating fee; 300 free listings/month then 35p. Buyer pays Buyer Protection fee: £0.10 fixed + 7% of first £20 + 4% of £20.01-£300 + 2% of £300-£4,000 (fixed part cut from £0.75 to £0.10 in July 2025, per search summary). Non-UK private sellers: 12.8% + 30p plus 0.42% regulatory fee (trainers >= £100: 8% + 30p).

ebay_ireland.note: Not researched/found; Irish sellers mostly use eBay.ie (EU fees) or Vinted/DoneDeal.

ebay_canada.seller_fee: Clothing, Shoes & Accessories 13.6% + C$0.30-0.40 per order; athletic shoes >= C$150 8% no per-order fee. Applies to total incl. shipping and GST/HST.

us.itemizing: Generally must itemize on Schedule A to deduct a charitable contribution.
us.condition: 'You can't take a deduction for clothing or household items you donate unless the clothing or household items are in good used condition or better.' Exception: a single item not in good used condition may be deducted if claimed at more than $500 with a qualified appraisal and Form 8283 Section B.
us.valuation: Fair market value; 'The price that buyers of used items actually pay in used clothing stores, such as consignment or thrift shops, is an indication of the value.'
us.form_8283: Required when noncash deductions total more than $500. Section A: items/groups claimed at $5,000 or less. Section B: over $5,000 (and the not-in-good-condition clothing case over $500).
us.non_itemizer_2026: From tax year 2026 (OBBBA) non-itemizers may deduct up to $1,000 ($2,000 joint) of CASH gifts to public charities; noncash gifts such as clothing do not qualify.
us.goodwill_value_guides: Regional Goodwill affiliates publish their own ranges, e.g. men's shirt ~$3-12, women's dress ~$6-25 (aggregated by a third-party guide; affiliates differ).

uk.rule: No income-tax deduction for the donor on donated goods. Under Retail Gift Aid the charity shop sells goods as the donor's agent; net proceeds are treated as a Gift Aid donation, letting the charity reclaim 25p per £1 from HMRC (e.g. goods sold for £25 are worth ~£31 to the charity). Donor must be a UK income/capital-gains taxpayer and sign a declaration.

ireland.rule: Charitable Donation Scheme applies only to donations of money (or designated securities) totalling at least €250 and at most €1m a year; goods are not eligible. No relief for donated clothing.

canada.rule: Gifts in kind can earn an official donation receipt at fair market value, but many thrift charities do not issue receipts for ordinary used clothing; one charity thrift operator states receipts only where combined FMV is $500 or more (charity policy, not a CRA threshold).
canada.note: CRA's own page was not read; treat as low confidence.

mexico.rule: Donations (including in kind) to SAT-authorised donatarias are deductible for individuals up to 7% of the prior year's accumulable income; an in-kind gift needs a CFDI stating description and value.

eu.name: EN 13402
eu.note: Labels by body dimensions in cm with pictograms; primary dimension: chest/bust for jackets and women's shirts, waist for trousers, neck for men's shirts; women's bust 76-152 cm in 4 cm steps. Letter codes e.g. women M = 90-98 cm bust, L = 98-107 cm.

us.name: ASTM D5585 (women's misses body measurements; voluntary; the commercial standard sizes were withdrawn by NBS in 1983)
us.note: Sizes are not legally standardised; brands vanity-size.

uk_ireland.name: UK dress sizes (Ireland uses UK sizes); EN 13402 also adopted as BS EN 13402
uk_ireland.note: UK women's = US women's + 4 (M&S: US/CAN 2 = UK 6 = EU 34).

canada.name: Same numeric sizes as US for clothing and shoes

mexico.name: NMX standards (voluntary): NMX-A-102-INNTEX size designation; NMX-A-23 women's/girls' outerwear; NMX-A-45 men's/boys' outerwear
mexico.note: Women's numeric sizes 26, 28, 30 ... 48 correspond to US 2, 4, 6 ... 24 (MX = US + 24). Men's letters ECH, CH, M, G, EG, EEG. Footwear in cm of foot length.

womens_dresses_tops.rule: US = UK - 4 = EU - 32 (French/Spanish EU numbering; German EU runs 2 lower, not covered here) = MX - 24

mens_trousers.rule: US, Canada, UK, Ireland and Mexico label waist and inseam in inches (e.g. 32x32). French/Italian EU size = waist in inches + 16 (32" = EU 48); German/Scandinavian brands may label waist in cm.
mens_trousers.mexico_note: Mexican men's trousers commonly labelled in inch-based waist numbers (search summary: men's numbers 36-46 for shirts/outerwear). Not confirmed against an NMX table.

mens_shirts_collar.rule: US/UK/IE/CA/MX label neck in inches; EU labels neck in cm; Italian brands use jacket-style numbers.

source.note: Oliver Spencer chart hosted by Nordstrom. 15.75" = 40 cm is the usual missing step.

formulas_wikipedia.Mexico_practice: Retail practice: Mexican adult size equals foot length in cm (e.g. 24 = US women 7; 24.5 = US women 7.5). The Wikipedia formula and the cm practice disagree; use the cm practice for retail labels.

clarks_uk_table_women.us_women_note: US women ≈ UK + 2 (Wikipedia formula); Clarks' own UK page omits US.

clarks_uk_table_men.us_men_note: US men ≈ UK + 1 (Wikipedia formula; a search summary of Clarks charts gives UK 6 = US 7, UK 9 = US 10).

canada.height_note: StatCan's article gives no mean height. Search summaries cite ~175 cm men / ~162 cm women from CHMS but no StatCan table was read; recorded as null. CHMS Cycle 2 height table exists: https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/n1/pub/82-626-x/2012001/t023-eng.htm (not read).

mexico.published_facts: ENSANUT 2022: 75.2% of adults 20+ overweight or obese (women 76.8%, men 73.5%); abdominal obesity cut-offs waist >= 80 cm women, >= 90 cm men; ~80% above cut-off.
mexico.note: No mean height or mean waist by sex found in an ENSANUT publication. News articles cite 'INEGI' means of 1.69-1.70 m men and 1.56-1.58 m women without a traceable table; not recorded.

Los Angeles and Vancouver cobblers: no current published price list from a shop inside the city; LA figure is a 2013 article, Vancouver resole figures are forum/blog quotes.
Toronto cobbler figures are from ShoeMedic in Oakville (GTA), not the City of Toronto.
Turnaround days published by only a few shops (Mid City NYC 10-14 business days; Michael Andrews 7-14; San Pedro 4-7; 1 Stop Wash 2-4; Love Your Tailor <=7; El Zapatitos 3-5).
Several official fee pages were blocked (Poshmark, Depop, ThredUp); their fee schedules are search-summary only.
No authoritative resale-value-to-retail ratio or time-to-sell data exists from platforms; only blog estimates.
Uniqlo, Zara and men's retailer charts not retrieved.
Mexico has no published ENSANUT mean height/waist; Canada mean height not read from a StatCan table; Ireland's latest measured data is 2008-2010.
